MythosMini is a small language model ("mini Fable") built in Python 3.12. This file is the contract for any agent working here. Read it fully, then read `journal.md` before starting any task. Detailed procedures live in `docs/rules/` — read the relevant one before doing that kind of work; they are part of this contract, not optional extras.

Alright, I’ve just kicked off the training run with the command:

```bash
timeout 75 python3 train.py 2 4 2>&1 | tail -40
```

The tool response tells me the process is now running in the background (ID b01o94n7g) and its stdout/stderr is being streamed into a temporary file:

```
/tmp/claude-1000/-home-lane-MythosMini/471accf0-3df7-4e2e-a567-a094f8f8d585/tasks/b01o94n7g.output
```

My goal, as per the user’s request, is to “train the model for 60 s, look at the tokens per second (tps)”. The training script prints periodic status updates (usually every few seconds) that include the number of tokens processed and the elapsed time, from which I can compute tps. However, I don’t have those numbers yet because the process just started.

I need to wait long enough for the training script to generate a few status lines, but not so long that the 75‑second timeout expires and the process ends before I can read the output. A 40‑second pause seems reasonable: it gives the script about half the allotted time to produce multiple log lines (the script typically logs every ~5–10 seconds), yet leaves ~35 seconds remaining before the timeout kills it. This way I can safely read the intermediate output without interfering with the running process, satisfying the user’s “do not kill any running processes” constraint.

The sandbox environment lets me read the temporary output file directly. I’ll issue a `cat` after a `sleep 40` so that the command blocks for 40 seconds, then reads whatever has been written to the file up to that point. Using a single Bash command with a semicolon ensures the two actions happen sequentially in the same shell, keeping the tool call simple.

Thus, the next step is to execute:

```bash
sleep 40; cat /tmp/claude-1000/-home-lane-MythosMini/471accf0-3df7-4e2e-a567-a094f8f8d585/tasks/b01o94n7g.output
```

This will give me the mid‑run logs I need to extract the tokens‑per‑second metric without terminating the training job.
